general.q: Which African country is surrounded almost entirely by Senegal, except for its short Atlantic coastline?
general.why: The Gambia follows the path of the Gambia River and forms a narrow enclave inside Senegal.

general.q: What type of nut is ground down to form the main ingredient in traditional marzipan?
general.why: Marzipan is made primarily of sugar, honey, and ground almonds, often enhanced with almond extract.

general.q: What is the nearest major spiral galaxy to the Milky Way?
general.why: Andromeda is roughly 2.5 million light-years away and is on a collision course with the Milky Way.

general.q: Which is the only mammal capable of true, sustained flight?
general.why: While flying squirrels and sugar gliders can only glide, bats flap their wings for powered flight.

general.q: Which structural protein is the most abundant in the human body?
general.why: Collagen makes up about 30% of the body's total protein content, forming connective tissues.

pop.q: In the Channel 4 sitcom The IT Crowd, what is the name of the corporation where the main characters work?
pop.why: Reynholm Industries is the fictional London company where Denholm and later Douglas Reynholm act as bosses.

pop.q: In the Crash Bandicoot video game series, what is the name of the floating wooden tiki mask that protects Crash?
pop.why: Aku Aku acts as a protective guardian for Crash Bandicoot, granting invincibility when three are collected.

pop.q: Which iconic toy range introduced moving 'Eagle Eyes' controlled by a lever on the back of the figure's head in 1976?
pop.why: Action Man added 'Eagle Eyes' in 1976, allowing kids to slide a head lever to make the figure look side to side.

pop.q: In the 1985 sci-fi classic Back to the Future, what speed in miles per hour must the DeLorean reach to time travel?
pop.why: Doc Brown's modified DeLorean DMC-12 needs to hit exactly 88 mph to trigger the flux capacitor and jump through time.

pop.q: In the long-running BBC sci-fi series Doctor Who, what is the name of the Doctor's home planet?
pop.why: Gallifrey is the home world of the Time Lords, famous for its shining orange skies and silver trees.

music.q: What was the title of Alanis Morissette's smash-hit 1995 album featuring 'Ironic' and 'You Oughta Know'?
music.why: Jagged Little Pill became one of the best-selling albums of all time, selling over 33 million copies worldwide.

music.q: Which group spent four weeks at UK Number 1 in 2006 with the hit single 'I Don't Feel Like Dancin''?
music.why: Co-written with Elton John, the disco-pop track was the lead single from Scissor Sisters' second album, Ta-Dah.

music.q: Which glam rock band secured the UK Christmas Number 1 single in 1973 with 'Merry Xmas Everybody'?
music.why: Slade famously beat Wizzard's 'I Wish It Could Be Christmas Everyday' to claim the 1973 festive top spot.

music.q: Which synth-pop group released the acclaimed 1984 debut album 'The Age of Consent', featuring 'Smalltown Boy'?
music.why: Bronski Beat's debut album reached number 4 in the UK album charts and contained the hit single Smalltown Boy.

music.q: Which pop-punk band ran through the streets naked in the iconic music video for their 1999 hit 'What's My Age Again?'?
music.why: The video featured the band running through Los Angeles and became one of MTV's most played clips of 1999.

mix.q: In the Channel 4 sitcom Peep Show, what is the name of the flat block where Mark and Jez live?
mix.why: Apollo House in Croydon served as the iconic setting for Mark and Jez's shared flat in Peep Show.

mix.q: Which Welsh rock band released the hit album Performance and Cocktails in 1999?
mix.why: Stereophonics topped the UK album chart in 1999 with Performance and Cocktails.

mix.q: Which European capital city is built across 14 islands connected by more than 50 bridges?
mix.why: Stockholm stretches across an archipelago of 14 islands where Lake Mälaren meets the Baltic Sea.

mix.q: In the 1998 movie The Truman Show, what is the name of the idyllic island town where Truman lives?
mix.why: Truman Burbank lives his enclosed, televised life inside the constructed town of Seahaven.

mix.q: Which gas makes up the primary component of natural gas used in domestic heating?
mix.why: Methane accounts for around 70 to 90 percent of natural gas composition.

mix.q: Which synth-pop band spent five weeks at UK number one in 1984 with their debut single Relax?
mix.why: Frankie Goes to Hollywood topped the UK charts for five weeks with Relax despite a BBC radio ban.

mix.q: What is the name of the fictional realm in which most games in The Legend of Zelda series take place?
mix.why: Hyrule is the primary fantasy setting for Link's adventures throughout The Legend of Zelda franchise.

mix.q: Which King of England was deposed during the Glorious Revolution of 1688?
mix.why: King James II was deposed in 1688 and replaced by his daughter Mary II and her husband William III.

mix.q: Which American punk-rock band released the hit concept album American Idiot in 2004?
mix.why: Green Day scored a massive global hit with their 2004 rock opera American Idiot.

mix.q: In the BBC comedy series Gavin & Stacey, what is the surname of Bryn, played by Rob Brydon?
mix.why: Uncle Bryn's full name in Gavin & Stacey is Bryn West, brother-in-law to Stacey's mother Gwen.
